clue.text: Oppose the others crossing island

indicators.note: one thing crossing another sits athwart it, so one word is laid across the middle of the other

parts.note: the rest are the others, the remainder
Is is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A lone dissenter opposes everyone else's plan to cross over to an island.
explanation.walkthrough: The island's letters do not wrap the outside of the other word neatly; they go in just before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To resist something is to stand against it, a direct synonym of oppose as a verb.

clue.text: Bird of prey and rail on rocky height

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece placed on another sits above it, so the first part comes before the second

parts.note: to rail at someone is to scold them, as is to rap them
a tor is a rocky hilltop, as on Dartmoor in England

explanation.surface: A hawk perched on a rail atop a craggy summit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rail' looks like a fence or a bird (the rail is a waterbird), but here it is the verb meaning to complain angrily.
explanation.definitionFit: Raptor is the general term for hawks, eagles, falcons and other hunting birds with talons.

clue.text: Pils drunk at very loud joint

indicators.note: someone drunk is all over the place, so these letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: Pils is a pilsner lager; its letters are rearranged
ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: Lager is drunk at a noisy pub, a joint with very loud music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' reads as a bar or club, but it is the definition in its slang sense of a cannabis cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: Spliff is slang for a hand-rolled cannabis cigarette, which is also called a joint.

clue.text: Phone clubs in Naples, possibly — a daily might do this

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters could be arranged another way
one thing set in another lies inside it, so the first pieces go within the other

parts.note: the city's letters are reordered
to ring someone is to phone them
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: Someone telephones nightclubs in an Italian city, while a cleaner gets on with the housework.
explanation.walkthrough: A daily is British for a cleaning lady who comes in each day to do housework.
explanation.definitionFit: A domestic cleaner would give a home a thorough top-to-bottom scrub, which is to spring-clean it.

clue.text: Aromatic plant, heavenly by front of arboretum

parts.note: angelic means like the angels of heaven

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of arboretum

explanation.surface: A sweet-smelling, heavenly plant grows by the entrance to a tree garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Angelica is a fragrant umbellifer whose candied stems are used in baking, so it is a scented herb.

clue.text: Recklessly bold hunter, man fording river in county

indicators.note: doing something recklessly means without care or order, so the letters are thrown about
someone fording a stream has the water passing between them, so one piece crosses through the other

parts.note: these three words provide the letters to be rearranged
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A daring hunter wades across a river somewhere in the English shires.
explanation.walkthrough: The river's letter slots into the rearranged letters after their first two. Northumberland is England's northernmost county, on the Scottish border.
explanation.definitionFit: Northumberland is one of the English counties, so county is its category.

clue.text: Chopped vegetable served up with fish

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means reading from the bottom, so the word runs the other way
something chopped has had its end cut off, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a leek is an onion-family vegetable

explanation.surface: Diced vegetables come to the table alongside a fish dish.
explanation.walkthrough: LEEK loses its K to give LEE, which is then read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The eel is a long snakelike fish, so fish is its category.

clue.text: Let pro in that could form crime unit

indicators.note: letters that could form something else can be rearranged to make it

parts.note: these three words provide the eight letters

explanation.surface: Admitting a professional who could help form a new police squad.
explanation.definitionFit: Interpol is the international police organisation coordinating cross-border criminal investigations, a crime-fighting body.

clue.text: More than anything else done mostly during a formal dance

indicators.note: something happening during an event falls within it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: something done is over, finished

explanation.surface: What someone wants most is to have finished business while at a grand ball.
explanation.walkthrough: The shortened word goes inside the dance just after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Above all is an idiom meaning most importantly, ahead of every other consideration.

clue.text: Move some furniture apart in play

definitions.meaning: first meaning: tables set apart from each other
second meaning: the 1954 play by Terence Rattigan

explanation.surface: Stagehands shift furniture about during a theatre production.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition describes the action loosely: moving furniture apart leaves tables separate. Rattigan's play is set among the lonely residents of a seaside hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: Separate Tables is the title of a Terence Rattigan drama, and the phrase also literally describes tables placed apart.

clue.text: Missile is fired next to stand, a big brute

indicators.note: someone fired is dismissed, so the little word is sacked from the longer one

parts.note: Polaris was a submarine-launched nuclear missile
to bear something is to stand or tolerate it

explanation.surface: A rocket is launched beside a stand, making a terrifying brute of a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fired' wants to mean launching the missile, but it means the letters IS are dismissed from POLARIS.
explanation.definitionFit: The polar bear is the largest land carnivore, a huge and dangerous animal, so a big brute.

clue.text: Free, travel permit initially

indicators.note: initially here means placed at the beginning, putting the second-named word first

parts.note: to let is to permit
to go is to travel

explanation.surface: A free travel pass, a permit issued at the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' looks like a first-letter signal, but it only tells you the word for permit comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: To let go is to release, a phrasal verb matching free used as a verb.

clue.text: Composer from city on the River Main

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Jacques ..., composer of operettas such as Orpheus in the Underworld
second meaning: a German city beside Frankfurt

explanation.surface: A musician hailing from a German riverside town.
explanation.walkthrough: The composer took his surname from his father's birthplace, Offenbach am Main, so both meanings are linked.
explanation.definitionFit: Offenbach names both the French-German operetta writer and the Hessian city on the Main river.

clue.text: Gravity shown in portentous song of mourning

indicators.note: something shown in another thing appears inside it, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: dire can mean ominous, foreboding disaster
g is the symbol for acceleration due to gravity

explanation.surface: Solemnity is displayed in an ominous lament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gravity' reads as solemnity, matching the funeral scene, but it is the physics symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirge is a slow lament for the dead, sung or played at a funeral.

clue.text: Impractical theorist carried it on, implausibly

indicators.note: an implausible version is not a true one, so the letters are told in a different order

parts.note: these three words provide the eleven letters

explanation.surface: An unrealistic idealist persisted with an unlikely notion.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctrinaire, as a noun, is someone who applies a theory rigidly regardless of practical reality.

clue.text: Where Roedean girls may be sent for a spell?

definitions.text: Where Roedean girls may be sent for a spell?

parts.words: Where Roedean girls may be sent for a spell?
parts.note: surface reading: Roedean is an exclusive English girls' boarding school, so this seems to ask where its pupils might go for a while
setter's reading: a spell is a magic charm, and a finishing establishment teaches poise and grace

explanation.walkthrough: 'Spell' means a stretch of time in the surface, but a magic spell is a charm, pointing to the place that teaches young women deportment.
explanation.definitionFit: A charm school is a finishing establishment teaching etiquette and graceful manners to young women.

clue.text: Sleep soundly by fire in a sort of bag

indicators.note: soundly here means by sound, so what is heard counts rather than the spelling

parts.note: a nap is a short sleep; knap, to chip flint, is pronounced the same
to fire someone is to sack them

explanation.surface: Someone sleeps deeply beside a campfire, curled up in a sleeping bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sleep soundly' reads as sleeping well; 'soundly' actually means the word for a doze is heard, not spelt.
explanation.definitionFit: A knapsack is a bag carried on the back, a type of rucksack.

clue.text: Hag brought in by son could make one start

indicators.note: something brought in by another is carried inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: taken as written
a hag is an old witch

explanation.surface: A boy brings home an ugly old crone, which could give anyone a fright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start' looks like a jump of fright, but it means getting a machine going.
explanation.definitionFit: To switch on a device is to activate it with a switch, making it start working.

clue.text: Miles away, we hear, on manoeuvres round about the start of November

indicators.note: troops on manoeuvres move about, so the letters are moved into a new order
going round something encloses it, so the rearranged letters wrap the other pieces

parts.note: these words provide the letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, which is taken alone

parts.note: re means about, concerning
the opening letter of November

explanation.surface: Reports of distant army exercises taking place around early November.
explanation.walkthrough: 'We hear' looks like a sound-alike signal, but it is simply part of the letters to rearrange. RE and N sit together inside the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Nowhere near is an idiom for far off, matching the informal sense of miles away.

clue.text: Push forcefully through American street

parts.note: thru is the informal American spelling of through
St is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: Shoving your way along a busy US street.
explanation.definitionFit: To thrust is to drive or shove something with sudden force.

clue.text: One male ordered deep hamper

indicators.note: ordered means put into a fresh arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
M is the abbreviation for male
the letters of deep are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man orders a deep picnic basket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamper' looks like a basket, but it is the verb meaning to obstruct.
explanation.definitionFit: To impede is to hinder or obstruct progress, a synonym of the verb hamper.

clue.text: Iron peg in mine, short one

indicators.note: short means lacking something, so the final letter is cut off

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
taken as written, then shortened

explanation.surface: An iron peg left in a mine, one short of the full set.
explanation.definitionFit: A piton is a metal spike that climbers drive into rock cracks to anchor ropes.

clue.text: She wrote detective stories, some rivalling Hammett

indicators.note: some means only a portion, so the answer is part of the following letters

parts.note: runs from inside the first word into the second

explanation.surface: A female crime writer whose books are as good as some of Dashiell Hammett's.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters span riv-ALLING HAM-mett. Margery Allingham created the detective Albert Campion.
explanation.definitionFit: Margery Allingham was an English novelist of the golden age of crime fiction, famed for her Campion mysteries.

clue.text: Notice wine's in short supply for this special purpose

indicators.note: something in short supply is lacking a bit, so the final letter is removed

parts.note: an ad, advertisement, is a notice
hock is British for a German white wine from the Rhine

explanation.surface: A sign warns that wine is running low.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'is', linking the wine to its shortage.
explanation.definitionFit: Ad hoc is Latin meaning literally for this, describing something arranged for one particular purpose.

clue.text: John in prison

definitions.meaning: first meaning: American slang for a toilet
second meaning: slang for a jail

explanation.walkthrough: 'John' looks like a man's name, an inmate perhaps, but both words are slang for the same short word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for both a lavatory and a jail, so it serves both meanings.

clue.text: What could be outlined around Greenwich, initially?

definitions.text: What could be outlined around Greenwich, initially?

indicators.note: could be suggests a possible alternative form, so the letters are rearranged
around means encircling, so the rearranged letters wrap the extra letter

parts.note: the letters of outlined are rearranged

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word beside it

parts.note: the opening letter of Greenwich

explanation.surface: Asking what might be marked out on the map around Greenwich.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: the prime meridian, zero degrees of this, runs through Greenwich in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Longitude is measured from the Greenwich meridian, so lines of it are drawn on maps around Greenwich.

clue.text: Head after type showing benevolence

indicators.note: after means coming later, so the first-named word goes second

parts.note: a kind is a type or sort
a ness is a headland, as in Dungeness or Sheerness

explanation.surface: A boss following the sort of person who shows goodwill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' looks like a boss, but it is a headland; ness appears in British place names such as Dungeness.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindness is the quality of being generous and considerate, which is what benevolence means.

clue.text: Take up residence in N Yorks town

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to make a home somewhere
second meaning: a market town in North Yorkshire, England

explanation.surface: Moving to a town in North Yorkshire to live.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle is to establish a home somewhere, and Settle is also a small market town in the Yorkshire Dales.
